name: BiSeNet face parsing
plain: BiSeNet face parsing (Yu et al., ECCV 2018; zllrunning's face-parsing.PyTorch checkpoint as shipped by facexlib): labels skin, brows, eyes, glasses, ears, nose, mouth, lips, neck, cloth, hair and hat in a face crop (19 classes, CelebAMask-HQ). MIT code and weights.
summary: BiSeNet (Yu et al. 2018) face parsing from face-parsing.PyTorch: a ResNet-18 context path with attention refinement and feature fusion, 19 CelebAMask-HQ face-part classes (skin, brows, eyes, glasses, ears, earrings, nose, mouth, lips, neck, necklace, cloth, hair, hat) on a 512 x 512 face crop. The parser that GFPGAN / CodeFormer pipelines use through facexlib; MIT code and weights.

papers.title: BiSeNet: Bilateral Segmentation Network for Real-time Semantic Segmentation

official.reason: The network and the 79999_iter checkpoint are face-parsing.PyTorch's; facexlib carries them with a pinned GitHub release URL (the original is a Google Drive file). The test protocol (512 x 512 PIL bilinear, ImageNet normalisation, net(x)[0]) is test.py's.

limitations: No accuracy measurement: face parsing is scored on CelebAMask-HQ, which is not part of the evaluation data here (no public mirror with a clear licence); tiers are compared by output parity and speed only.
task_io: Input: one RGB image. Output: per-pixel class labels (logits with `logits=True`).

variants.name: bisenet-face-parsing

licence.training_note: face-parsing.PyTorch train.py: CelebAMask-HQ (non-commercial research only), ResNet-18 initialised from torchvision's ImageNet weights.

variants.input_size: any H x W >= 1, resized or padded inside the model

original16.protocol: median of 5 after 3 warm-up, uint8 CUDA input, original code at the pinned commit, torch.no_grad; peak = max over the first call and the timed calls
original16.note: .half() on 1 modules, fp16 inputs; face-parsing.PyTorch test.py: PIL resize 512 x 512 on the CPU, Normalize, net(x)[0], float32

portable.protocol: first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

quality.title: LaPa test (2,000 images), common face parts, mIoU / aAcc %
quality.protocol: Scores use one pixel confusion matrix across the split. Left and right eyes share one class, and left and right brows share one class. Labels outside the eight shared foreground classes count as background.

portable32.note: mIoU includes background and averages classes with at least one labelled or predicted pixel.

parity.text: CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 2.6e-05 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.0042 and p99 <= 0.02 (absolute error of the output `logits`).
